title: oncall-handoff-draft-amelia-fernandez
content:
Shift: 2024-10-03 19:00 - 2024-10-04 07:00 PT
Owner: Amelia Fernandez (eng-sre)
Handoff to: Noah Thompson at 07:00 PT

High-level summary:
- Quiet night overall. One transient alert for redis-cache-eu (partial replica lag) around 01:23 PT — recovered after failover and replica resync.
- A handful of short-lived 5xx spikes on hosted-api-prod at 03:10 PT correlated with a rollout of model-redwood-v2 in us-west; rollback to redwood-v1 fixed errors. Follow-up ticket created.
- No pager escalations to Weekends SRE pager.

Open incidents / follow-ups (actionable):
1) JIRA-SRV-412: hosted-api 5xx spike during model-redwood-v2 rollout
   - Summary: traffic saw increased 500s (ramp) immediately after canary reached 20% traffic. Error rates returned to baseline after rollback. Suspect model incompatibility with some kernel path on specific GPU type.
   - Priority: P2 (investigate in next business day)
   - Next steps: coordinate with eng-serving-runtime + Applied ML to repro on dedicated-staging. Ask release owner (tag: @maya-singh) for canary config and model binary.

2) Redis replica lag (redis-cache-eu) — transient
   - Timeline: 01:23 PT alert fired for replica lag > 5s, partial failover executed, primary remained healthy, replica rejoined and caught up by 01:48 PT.
   - Mitigation: automated failover succeeded. No data loss.
   - Action: monitor for increased frequency. If it repeats 3x in 24h open JIRA-SRV-419 and consider increasing replica_io_threads in redis conf for eu cluster.

Temporary procedures I followed (notes to future oncall):
- If you see cpu pressure on inference-hosts (gpu-device 0 at 99% usage but host CPU > 85%) — check for runaway batching controller:
  - kubectl -n inference get pods | grep batching-controller
  - kubectl -n inference logs deploy/batching-controller -c controller --since=2h | tail -n 200
  - If controller is requeuing > 1000/s, scale down by editing HPA or patch deployment: kubectl -n inference scale deploy/batching-controller --replicas=1 then file a ticket for engineering to adjust rate limits.

- Rollback procedure for model rollout (quick checklist):
  1) Open Console -> Rollouts -> select hosted-api route -> revert to previous model version (redwood-v1).
  2) Confirm canary traffic drops to 0% and monitor 5xx for next 10m.
  3) If errors continue, flip routing policy to route all traffic to dedicated fallback pool (policy: fallback-to-dedicated-us-west).
  4) Document timestamps in incident ticket.

Escalation contacts (order):
- On-call Engineer (primary): eng-sre pager (Slack #sre-oncall)
- Serving Runtime lead: Maya Singh (pager/Slack)
- Applied ML (model owner): Priya Menon (Slack)
- Infra: Riley Thompson (pager)
- Eng Manager (urgent): Samir Ali

Useful checks / quick commands:
- System health dashboards: Console -> Observability -> per-route latency/cost -> hosted-api-prod
- Check pods with restarts in last 2h: kubectl -n default get pods --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide | grep -E "CrashLoopBackOff|Error"
- Redis cluster health (eu): redis-cli -h redis-eu-primary info replication
- K8s node pressure: kubectl get nodes -o wide | awk '{print $1,$2,$7,$8}'

Notes / TODOs I left for engineering after tonight:
- Investigate kernel mismatch for redwood-v2 on NVidia A10x (likely quantization path) — assigned to eng-serving-runtime team.
- Add a Simulated Traffic Canary test in CI that runs small inference workload for each model rollout to dedicated-staging before canary.
- Tighten alerting: reduce noise for redis replica lag transient (< 10 minutes) but ensure escalation if failover occurs.

Known quirks / context to remember:
- eu-redis cluster has historically been sensitive during nightly backups (snapshot job at 00:30 PT). If you see lag alerts ~00:30 consider backup overlap.
- hosted-api route has a fallback policy to dedicated pools in us-west; that is often used during model rollouts if latency spikes.

Unresolved questions / discussion points:
- Do we want to automatically halt canary progression if 5xx rate increases by > 0.5% within first 10m? (Proposed: yes, but needs product sign-off.)
- Is adding a small preflight inference load in CI acceptable cost-wise for each PR? (Talk to infra + cost engineering.)

Personal notes / things I scribbled:
- Possible quick fix for redis: tweak client-side timeout for replication read to 1s for eu cluster. Need ops approval.
- If batching controller keeps requeuing, temporary set BATCH_MAX=32 env (lowers throughput but stabilizes latency).

If you take over this shift, ping me in #sre-oncall and I can walk through the logs. If anything looks urgent and you can't resolve, escalate to Maya -> Priya -> Riley in that order.

End of handoff.

-- Amelia
(leave any notes here in this doc for next oncall)
